bull.b: Extremely low leverage and a large equity/asset base give durable financial flexibility to fund R&D, commercial expansion and absorb clinical setbacks without immediate refinancing. This bolsters strategic optionality and reduces solvency risk over the next several quarters.

A sustained step-up in revenue and unusually high margins for biotech signal scalable commercial economics and improved operating discipline. Durable margin expansion supports reinvestment in pipeline and commercialization while increasing resilience to unit-cost variability.

Multiple near-term registrational readouts and a clear late-stage advancement plan materially broaden potential labeled indications. Successful readouts would structurally diversify revenue beyond the lead product and reduce single-product concentration over a multi-year horizon.

bear.b: Earnings-to-cash conversion remains inconsistent, with prior multi-year negative free cash flow and 2025 operating cash covering only two-thirds of net income. If growth or pricing pressure emerges, this variability could force slower R&D investment or external funding needs.

Elevated and rising R&D plus SG&A investment is necessary to pursue multiple indications but increases burn and requires sustained top-line growth to justify. Clinical setbacks or slower adoption would quickly pressure margins and cash runway decisions.

Heterogeneous indications and uncertain subset readouts raise the chance of delayed or inconclusive pivotal results. Combined with payer habits (IVIg prerequisites), successful label expansion and earlier-line uptake depend on positive, durable trial outcomes and slow-changing payer behavior.
